intro: String Python me text ka data type hai — 'Ahetesham', 'select * from users', 'RAG pipeline' sab strings hain. Ye immutable sequence hai, yani ek baar bana to uske andar ka character badla nahi ja sakta; har method nayi string return karta hai. Aage ke poore course me jo bhi input aayega (file, CSV, API JSON, LLM prompt) wo pehle string hi hota hai, isliye string manipulation aana matlab data cleaning, validation aur parsing aana.
theory: String ek ordered, immutable sequence hai Unicode characters ki. Index 0 se shuru hota hai, negative index peeche se ginta hai (-1 last character), aur s[i:j:k] slicing se sub-string banta hai.
Kyunki string immutable hai, s[0] = 'x' TypeError deta hai. 'Modify' karne ka matlab hamesha nayi string banana hai — isliye methods ka result store karna padta hai.

Methods kaafi hain par kaam ke groups: case (lower, upper, title, casefold), trim/pad (strip, lstrip, ljust), search (find, index, startswith, count), replace (replace, translate), split/join (split, rsplit, splitlines, join).
f-string (f'{name}') modern formatting hai: expression andar chalta hai, spec se rounding/width milti hai (f'{x:.2f}'), aur repr ke liye !r. Purane % aur .format() ab sirf legacy code me milte hain.

Escape sequences (\n, \t, \\, \') aur raw string (r'C:\new') ka fark yaad rakho — regex aur Windows paths me raw string hi sahi hai. Encoding ka default UTF-8 hai; multi-line text ke liye triple quotes use karo.
syntax:
s = 'Python'        # single quotes
s2 = "Python"       # double quotes — same cheez
tri = '''multi
line'''
raw = r'C:\new\test'  # backslash literal rehta hai

s[0]      # 'P'  — first character
s[-1]     # 'n'  — last character
s[1:4]    # 'yth' — start se pehle end tak
s[::-1]   # 'nohtyP' — reverse
s[::2]    # 'Pto'  — every second character

s.upper(); s.lower(); s.strip(); s.split(','); ','.join(parts)
s.replace('old', 'new'); s.find('th'); s.startswith('Py'); s.count('t')
f'{name} scored {score:.1f}'   # formatted insert

examples.code:
name = 'Ahetesham'
print(name[0], name[-1])
print(name[0:4])
print(len(name))
print(name.upper())
explain: name[0] pehla character deta hai, name[-1] last — Python negative index ko length se jodta hai, isliye -1 ka matlab len(name) - 1.
name[0:4] me end index include nahi hota, isliye 4 characters aate hain: 'Ahet'.
len(name) characters ki ginti deta hai (bytes nahi) — 'Ahetesham' me 9.
upper() original ko nahi badalta, nayi uppercase string return karta hai; immutable hone ki wajah se ye hamesha naya object hai.

examples.code:
raw = '  Python, SQL ,  pandas  '
skills = [s.strip().lower() for s in raw.split(',')]
print(skills)
print('|'.join(skills))
print(f'{skills[0].title()} — {len(skills)} skills')
print(raw.strip().replace('  ', ' '))
explain: split(',') har comma par todta hai aur spaces bhi saath le aata hai — isliye har tukde par strip() lagana zaroori hai.
casefold/lower lagane se 'SQL' aur 'sql' ek jaise ho jate hain; comparison ke liye ye normalization basic step hai.
'|'.join(skills) list ko wapas string banata hai — separator wo string hai jispar join call hua, list nahi.
f-string ke andar expression aur method call dono chalte hain: {skills[0].title()} aur {len(skills)}.
Aakhir me strip() bahar ke spaces hatata hai aur replace('  ',' ') andar ke double spaces single karta hai — typical clean-up pipeline.
re.sub ke saath negated character class [^a-z0-9\s] har non-alphanumeric ko space se badal deta hai — punctuation hat jata hai.
text.split() bina argument diye whitespace par todta hai aur duplicate spaces ignore karta hai, phir ' '.join se single-space version milta hai.
compress() run-length encoding hai: jab tak same character repeat ho raha hai count badhta hai.
f'{text[i-1]}{count}' wahi character plus count deta hai, par count 1 hone par sirf character likha jata hai — isliye 'abc' waisa hi rehta hai.
Loop len(text)+1 tak chalta hai taaki last run bhi flush ho jaye — boundary par ek extra iteration classic technique hai.

realWorld: Data cleaning: CSV/Excel se aaya ' Pune ' aur 'pune' ek hi city hai — strip + casefold + replace ka combo har ETL job me pehla step hota hai.
Log parsing: production log line se timestamp, level aur message nikaalna split/rsplit aur startswith se hota hai; isi par alerting banti hai.
PII masking: 'Ashu Khan' ya '9876543210' ko report/LLM prompt me bhejne se pehle mask karna padta hai (s[:3] + '*'*n) — compliance requirement hai.
Prompt building: LLM ke liye system + context + user message ko f-string/template se jodna padta hai, aur token limit ke hisab se truncate karna padta hai.

interview.q: Strings immutable kyun hain aur iska practical asar kya hai?
interview.a: Immutable hone se string ko hash kiya ja sakta hai (dictionary key ban sakti hai), multiple threads bina lock share kar sakte hain, aur interned short strings memory bachate hain. Asar: har 'change' nayi string banata hai, isliye loop me s += x karne se O(n^2) ho jata hai — wahan list + join use karo.
interview.tip: Answer me hashability aur thread-safety dono mention karo, sirf 'change nahi kar sakte' mat kaho.

interview.q: == aur is me string comparison me kya fark hai?
interview.a: == value compare karta hai (character by character), is identity compare karta hai (same object). CPython chhoti literal strings ko intern karta hai, isliye 'ab' is 'ab' aksar True milega — par ye guarantee nahi hai. Kabhi bhi identity par bharosa karke string equality mat likho; sirf identity check ke liye is use karo.
interview.tip: Interviewer yahan interned behaviour ka edge case sunna chahta hai — 'aksar True, par guaranteed nahi' bolna strong answer hai.

interview.q: s[::-1] kaise reverse karta hai?
interview.a: Slice syntax start:stop:step hai. Jab start aur stop khaali ho aur step -1 ho, Python end se shuru karke 1-1 peeche chalta hai, isliye poora string reverse milta hai. Ye O(n) hai aur ek nayi string banati hai.
interview.tip: Slice ka default (start=0, stop=len, step=1) mention karo — interviewers basics ka clarity test karte hain.

interview.q: Loop me string concatenation slow kyun hai aur alternative kya hai?
interview.a: String immutable hai, isliye har += nayi string banata hai aur purana content copy hota hai — n iterations par O(n^2). Sahi tarika: parts ki list banao aur ' '.join(parts) se ek hi allocation me jodo, jo O(n) hai.
interview.tip: Real numbers do: 100k strings par += seconds leta hai jabki join milliseconds.

interview.q: split() aur split(' ') me kya fark hai?
interview.a: Bina argument split() whitespace ke har run par todta hai aur empty strings nikaal deta hai, isliye multiple spaces aur tabs ignore ho jate hain. split(' ') exactly ek space par todta hai, isliye consecutive spaces se khali strings aa jati hain — clean data ke liye pehla safer hai.
interview.tip: Isi logic se rsplit aur splitlines ke use case bhi bol dena.

interview.q: String formatting ke liye f-string vs .format() vs % — production me kya choose karoge?
interview.a: f-string: fast, readable, debug-friendly (f'{x=}'), par expression evaluate hote hain isliye user-controlled template ke saath injection ka dhyan rakhna padta hai. .format() tab jab template runtime par aaye (config/translation files). % sirf legacy logging code me; logging me actually lazy % style logger.info('%s', x) recommended hai taaki message format sirf zaroorat par ho.
interview.tip: Logging ka lazy-format point batao, ye practical depth dikhata hai.

beginner.a: s[::-1] ek step me reverse kar deta hai (O(n), nayi string).
beginner.explain: Negative step end se start ki taraf chalta hai, isliye start/stop khaali chhod do.
beginner.tip: Donon tarike batao — slice idiomatic hai, reversed() iterator deta hai.

beginner.q: String ki length find karo (spaces ke saath aur bina).
beginner.a: len(s) total characters deta hai; spaces hata kar ginti ke liye len(s.replace(' ', '')) ya sum(not c.isspace() for c in s) use karo.
beginner.commonMistake: len(s.strip()) se lagta hai spaces hat gaye, par strip sirf kinaron ke spaces hatata hai.

beginner.a: Ek set me vowels rakho aur character-wise check karo — set lookup O(1) hai, isliye overall O(n).
beginner.code:
s = 'Machine Learning'
vowels = set('aeiou')
print(sum(1 for c in s.lower() if c in vowels))

beginner.q: String me uppercase aur lowercase characters count karo.
beginner.a: c.isupper() aur c.islower() per-character check dete hai; ginti ke liye sum() ya loop use karo.
beginner.code:
s = 'PyThOn 3.14'
print(sum(c.isupper() for c in s), sum(c.islower() for c in s))
print(sum(c.isdigit() for c in s))
beginner.explain: bool int ki tarah sum ho jata hai: True = 1, False = 0 — ye idiom Python me common hai.

beginner.q: First aur last character find karo.
beginner.a: s[0] aur s[-1]. Empty string par IndexError aata hai, isliye pehle `if s:` check karo.
beginner.commonMistake: Bina guard s[0] likhna — empty input par crash.

beginner.q: Palindrome hai ya nahi check karo.
beginner.a: Normalize (lower + alphanumeric only) karke s == s[::-1] compare karo.
beginner.code:
def is_palindrome(s):
    clean = ''.join(c.lower() for c in s if c.isalnum())
    return clean == clean[::-1]

print(is_palindrome('Madam'))
print(is_palindrome('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'))
beginner.tip: Interview me yahi question 'ignore punctuation and case' ke saath aata hai — pehle normalization likho.

intermediate.q: String me duplicate characters find karo.
intermediate.a: collections.Counter se frequency lo aur count > 1 wale characters filter karo.
intermediate.code:
from collections import Counter

dupes = [c for c, n in Counter('programming').items() if n > 1]
print(sorted(dupes))

intermediate.a: Counter(s).most_common(1) ya max(counter, key=counter.get) — donon O(n).
intermediate.code:
from collections import Counter

c = Counter('machine learning')
print(c.most_common(2))
intermediate.explain: most_common ties ko insertion order me todta hai, isliye deterministic hai.

intermediate.q: Sentence ke words ka order reverse karo (characters nahi).
intermediate.a: split() se words list banao, reverse karo, aur ' '.join se jodo.

intermediate.q: String se duplicate characters remove karo, order preserve karke.
intermediate.a: Seen set rakho aur sirf naye characters append karo — O(n) aur order safe (set() alone order tod deta hai).
intermediate.code:
s = 'programming'
seen, out = set(), []
for ch in s:
    if ch not in seen:
        seen.add(ch)
        out.append(ch)
print(''.join(out))
intermediate.commonMistake: set(s) se order random ho jata hai — interview me 'preserve order' likha ho to ye galat hai.

intermediate.a: split + Counter; case normalize karna na bhoolo warna 'The' aur 'the' alag gine jayenge.
intermediate.code:
from collections import Counter

text = 'Data data science is data driven'
print(Counter(w.lower() for w in text.split()).most_common(3))

intermediate.q: Email format validate karo (regex ke bina bhi).
intermediate.a: Simple check: exactly ek '@', local aur domain dono non-empty, domain me '.' ho aur aakhri part 2+ characters ka. Regex copy-paste karne se pehle ye rules bolna interview me better lagta hai.
intermediate.tip: Real project me aakhri faisla server-side validation ka hota hai — client check sirf UX hai.

advanced.q: Custom string compression (run-length encoding) implement karo.
advanced.a: Consecutive same characters ka run count karke 'char+count' likho; count 1 ho to sirf character. O(n) time, O(n) space.
advanced.explain: Loop len(s)+1 tak isliye chalta hai taaki last run flush ho jaye.

advanced.q: Longest substring without repeating characters find karo.
advanced.a: Sliding window + last-seen index map: left pointer ko duplicate ke baad shift karo, har step par window length update karo. O(n) time.
advanced.tip: Brute force O(n^2) se shuru karke window par optimize karna interviewer ko pasand aata hai.

advanced.a: Har word ka sorted-characters ya character-count tuple key banake dictionary me group karo. Sorted key O(k log k) hai, count tuple O(k) — bade inputs par count tuple better.
advanced.code:
from collections import defaultdict

groups = defaultdict(list)
for w in ['eat', 'tea', 'tan', 'ate', 'nat', 'bat']:
    groups[''.join(sorted(w))].append(w)
print(sorted(groups.values()))

advanced.q: Text normalization system banao (punctuation, case, whitespace).
advanced.a: Lowercase → non-alphanumeric ko space → whitespace collapse. Ye idempotent hona chahiye: normalize(normalize(x)) == normalize(x).
advanced.explain: Idempotency NLP me zaroori hai — warna dobara process karne par data badalta rehta hai.

advanced.a: Sorted words par bisect se prefix ka insertion point dhoondo aur aage scan karke matches do; O(log n + k) milta hai. Yehi tarika SQL ke LIKE 'abc%' se sasta hai jab data memory me ho.
advanced.code:
from bisect import bisect_left

words = sorted(['rag', 'ranking', 'random', 'range', 'transformer'])

def autocomplete(prefix, limit=3):
    i = bisect_left(words, prefix)
    return [w for w in words[i:i + limit] if w.startswith(prefix)]

print(autocomplete('ran'))
print(autocomplete('ra'))

interview.q: Interview me poocha jaye: 'Ek 5 GB log file me ek keyword kitni baar aaya, nikalo' — string knowledge kaise use karoge?
interview.a: Poori file memory me mat lo; line by line padho aur per-line count += line.count(keyword) karo. Agar keyword line boundary par toot sakta hai to chunk overlap rakho. Agar multiple keywords hain to Aho-Corasick ya multi-pattern approach bolna depth dikhata hai.
interview.tip: Memory constraints pehle bolo, phir approach — interviewer yehi order sunna chahta hai.

interview.q: Interview: do strings 'same characters, different order' hain ya nahi — O(n) me batao.
interview.a: Counter(s1) == Counter(s2) O(n) hai; sorted comparison O(n log n) hai. Unicode/bade alphabet me counting array 26 se kaam nahi chalega, Counter safer hai.
interview.tip: Edge cases bolna: length mismatch, spaces, case sensitivity.

interview.q: Interview: string me first non-repeating character find karo.
interview.a: Ek pass me Counter, doosre pass me pehla character jiska count 1 ho — O(n) time, O(k) space.
interview.tip: Ordered pass zaroori hai — sirf Counter ka most_common se ye answer nahi milta.

interview.q: Interview: password strength checker likho aur batao kaunse string operations lagenge.
interview.a: length, any(c.isupper()), any(c.islower()), any(c.isdigit()), any(not c.isalnum()) — paanch checks. Result ko score me convert karo aur weak/medium/strong do. Regex se bhi ho sakta hai par multiple lookaheads readability todte hain.
interview.code:
def strength(p):
    score = sum([len(p) >= 8, any(c.isupper() for c in p), any(c.islower() for c in p), any(c.isdigit() for c in p), any(not c.isalnum() for c in p)])
    return ['very weak', 'weak', 'medium', 'medium', 'strong', 'very strong'][score]

print(strength('Ahetesham@2026'), strength('abcdef'))
interview.tip: Security interview me plain-text password store/log karne ka zikr bhi mat karo — hashing mention karo.

realworld.q: CSV header names ko database-friendly banado ('Monthly Revenue ($)' → 'monthly_revenue').
realworld.a: Lowercase → non-alphanumeric ko underscore → duplicate underscores collapse → kinare ke underscores strip. Ye idempotent hona chahiye.
realworld.code:
import re

def slug(name):
    s = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', name.lower()).strip('_')
    return s

print(slug('Monthly Revenue ($)'))
print(slug('  User-ID  '))

realworld.q: Log line '2026-09-24 10:31:02 ERROR db timeout' se level aur message nikalo.
realworld.a: split(maxsplit=3) se chaar hisse milte hain — date, time, level, message. Fixed positions par split safe hai kyunki message me spaces ho sakti hain.
realworld.code:
line = '2026-09-24 10:31:02 ERROR db timeout'
date, time, level, msg = line.split(maxsplit=3)
print(level, '|', msg)
print(line.startswith('2026'))
realworld.explain: maxsplit=3 exactly 4 hisse deta hai; message ke andar ke spaces safe rehte hain.

realworld.q: Customer name aur phone ko report/LLM prompt me mask karo.
realworld.a: Pehle kuch characters rakho, baaki '*'. Phone ke liye last 4 digits dikhana standard hai.

realworld.q: LLM prompt me context ko token limit ke andar kaise laoge?
realworld.a: Approximate tokens ≈ len(text) / 4 (English), isliye budget se characters nikaalo aur us se zyada context ko end se truncate karo — beginning me instruction rakho, kyunki models start/end par zyada dhyan dete hain. Exact count ke liye tokenizer use karo.
realworld.tip: Ye 'lost in the middle' problem hai — real interview me ye term bolna strong hai.

coding.question: Count vowels, consonants, digits aur spaces ek hi pass me.
coding.build: Function jo counts ka dictionary return kare.
coding.hint: Set banao vowels ka, phir c.isalpha() se consonant verify karo (vowel minus).
coding.explanation: Pehle vowel check karna zaroori hai, warna 'a' consonant group me chala jayega. elif chain single pass me sab classify karti hai.
coding.better: Bade text ke liye Counter(categorise(c) for c in s) se grouped counts milega, par single pass me memory kam lagti hai.
coding.followUp: 5 GB file par kaise karoge? (streaming, chunk overlap, multiprocessing)

coding.question: Palindrome checker likho jo punctuation aur case ignore kare.
coding.build: Function is_palindrome(text) -> bool, sirf alphanumeric compare.
coding.input: 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'
coding.hint: Pehle normalized string banao, phir slicing se reverse.
coding.solution:
def is_palindrome(text):
    clean = [c.lower() for c in text if c.isalnum()]
    return clean == clean[::-1]

print(is_palindrome('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'))
print(is_palindrome('Python Strings'))
coding.explanation: List of chars par comparison slice reverse se hoti hai; do pointers wala approach bhi O(n) hai par zyada code likhna padta hai.
coding.better: Bade input par left/right do pointer use karo — extra list nahi banti, space O(1).
coding.followUp: Sirf punctuation ignore karna ho par case na ho to change kya hoga?

coding.question: Run-length encoding aur decoding dono implement karo.
coding.build: encode(s) aur decode(s), dono round-trip par original wapas dein.
coding.expected: encode → 'a3bc4d' aur decode se original wapas
coding.hint: Decode me digits multi-digit ho sakte hain, isliye accumulate karo.
coding.explanation: Encode me last run flush karne ke liye loop len+1 tak jata hai. Decode me digit run ko accumulate karna zaroori hai warna 'a12' do characters samajh liya jayega.
coding.better: Decode ko index-based while loop ki jagah regex (\w)(\d*) findall se likh sakte hain — chhota code, same complexity.
coding.followUp: Best case me RLE compressed string badi ho jati hai — kab faayda, kab nuksan?

coding.question: Longest substring without repeating characters nikalo.
coding.hint: Sliding window: har character ka last index yaad rakho aur left pointer ko duplicate ke aage shift karo.
coding.concept: Sliding window over an immutable sequence
coding.explanation: last[ch] >= left check window se bahar ke purane occurrence ko ignore karta hai — iske bina left galat shift hota hai.
coding.better: Set-based version se bhi O(n) milta hai par set par remove karna padta hai; index map version ek pass me chalta hai.
coding.followUp: Agar at most k repeats allowed hon to kaise badaloge? (window + count map)

coding.question: Anagram groups banao aur har group ko alphabetical order me do.
coding.build: Function group_anagrams(words) → list of sorted groups.
coding.hint: Key ke liye sorted characters ya character-count tuple use karo.
coding.explanation: Canonical key se 'eat' aur 'tea' ek hi bucket me aate hain. Post-processing me groups aur unke andar ke words sort karna expected output deterministic banata hai.
coding.time: O(n · k log k), k = word length
coding.better: Counting tuple (26-tuple) key O(k) hai isliye bade words par sorted key se tez — Unicode ke liye Counter tuple.
coding.followUp: Streaming input (words aate rehte hain) par grouping kaise karoge?

coding.question: Text se top-N keywords nikalo stop words hata kar.
coding.build: Function top_keywords(text, n) → [(word, count)] frequency order me.
coding.input: Machine learning is a field of study and machine learning needs data
coding.hint: Normalize → split → stop word set se filter → Counter.
coding.explanation: strip('.,!?') punctuation hatata hai, lower case normalize karta hai, aur generator expression stop words ko counter tak pahunchne hi nahi deta.
coding.better: Stemming/lemmatization (learning → learn) se 'learning' aur 'learn' merge ho jate hain; bade corpora me regex tokenizer better.
coding.followUp: TF-IDF kya add karega frequency ke upar? (rare words ko weight)

coding.question: Caesar cipher (shift) implement karo aur shift-aware validation rakho.
coding.build: encrypt(text, shift) aur decrypt(text, shift) — sirf letters shift hon.
coding.hint: chr/ord se wrap karo: uppercase aur lowercase ka base alag hai.
coding.explanation: % 26 se z se aage wrap hota hai; base ord('A')/ord('a') alag rakhne se case preserve hota hai.
coding.better: str.translate + translate table banane se C-level speed milti hai — per-character Python loop hat jata hai.
coding.followUp: Frequency analysis is cipher ko kaise todti hai, aur modern encryption kya alag karti hai?

debugging.error: IndexError: string index out of range
debugging.why: Index 0-based hai, isliye last valid index len(word) - 1 = 5 hai. len(word) = 6 likhne se ek aage nikal jate hain.
debugging.fix: Last character ke liye word[-1] ya word[len(word) - 1] use karo.
debugging.lesson: Off-by-one string indexing me sabse common bug hai; negative index readability ke liye better hai.

debugging.error: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
debugging.why: Python weakly typed nahi hai — + do strings ko jodta hai, int ko automatic string nahi banata. Java/C# ka implicit conversion yahan nahi hota.
debugging.fix: f-string use karo ya str() se convert karo.
debugging.lesson: Number aur text jodte waqt hamesha f-string prefer karo — conversion, spacing aur readability teenon ek jagah.

debugging.why: Method ka naam galat likha gaya hai. Python attribute na milne par AttributeError deta hai — ise typo samajh kar silent skip nahi karta.
debugging.fix: Sahi method naam upper() use karo; editor ke autocomplete se typo avoid karo.
debugging.correct:
topic = 'Strings'
print(topic.upper())
print([m for m in dir(topic) if 'upper' in m])
debugging.lesson: Unknown attribute par AttributeError turant fail-fast hota hai — isi current failure ko catch karta hai, jabki alag attribute-call bhi karta hai.
debugging.explain: dir() se available methods dekho — guess karne se better hai.

debugging.error: Logic error: sab letters uppercase ho gaye, sirf pehla letter nahi
debugging.why: title case ka matlab har word ka pehla letter capital hai, poori string uppercase nahi. Koi exception nahi aata isliye ye logic bug hai — output galat hai par program chalta rehta hai.
debugging.fix: Har word par capitalize() lagao (ya .title() use karo).
debugging.lesson: Crash bug turant dikhta hai; logic bug chup rehta hai — isliye logic ke liye expected output ke saath test likhna zaroori hai.

debugging.error: TypeError: count() takes at least 1 argument (0 given)
debugging.why: str.count(sub) ka ek required argument hai. Bina argument call karne par Python TypeError deta hai, 'zero' return nahi karta.
debugging.fix: Count karna hai to substring/character do: s.count('n'). Poori length chahiye ho to len(s) use karo.
debugging.lesson: Method signature yaad ho to hi call karo; help(), docstring ya IDE hints se argument count confirm karna seconds bachata hai.

challenges.hint: reversed() iterator deta hai, join se string banega.
challenges.deliverable: Ek snippet + uski complexity ka comment.

challenges.prompt: Word-wrap function likho jo text ko given width par tode, words ko beech se na kaate, aur naye words ko next line par le jaye.
challenges.hint: Greedy: words ko line me jodo jab tak width cross na ho, phir flush karo.

challenges.prompt: Ek text 'diff' tool banao jo do strings ki line-by-line similarity report de (added, removed, % similar) bina external library ke.
challenges.hint: difflib.SequenceMatcher ration() deta hai; opcodes se change blocks nikalte hain.
challenges.deliverable: CLI script jo do files/two strings compare karke summary print kare.

projects.code:
def analyse(text):
    words = text.split()
    vowels = set('aeiou')
    counts = {
        'chars_with_spaces': len(text),
        'chars_no_spaces': len(text.replace(' ', '')),
        'words': len(words),
        'vowels': sum(1 for c in text.lower() if c in vowels),
        'sentences': sum(1 for c in text if c in '.!?'),
    }
    counts['avg_word_len'] = round(sum(len(w) for w in words) / len(words), 2) if words else 0
    return counts

report = analyse('Python strings are immutable. String methods return new objects!')
for k, v in report.items():
    print(f'{k:20} : {v}')
projects.explanation: Poora kaam ek function me hai taaki test karna aasan ho: input dena, dictionary lena, values assert karna. sentence count '.' '!' '?' par ginti hai — perfect nahi, par predictable.

projects.explanation: normalize() idempotent hai (dobara chalane par same output), isliye pipeline me safe hai. search() walrus operator se loop compact hai aur overlapping matches bhi pakadta hai. analysis() ek pure function hai — same input par same output, isliye test karna trivial.

interview.q: normalize() idempotent kyun hona chahiye?
interview.a: Agar function dobara chalane par output badalta rehta to pipeline har rerun par alag result deti aur debugging impossible ho jati. Idempotency test ek line me likha ja sakta hai.

interview.q: Counter ki jagah manual dictionary kyun nahi?
interview.a: Counter me most_common, arithmetic aur missing-key handling built-in hai; manual dict me default handling khud likhni padti hai. Interview me complexity same O(n) hai, Counter readability aur correctness dono deta hai.

interview.q: Problems ye module kaise solve karta hai jo Version 1 nahi karta tha?
interview.a: V1 raw text par ginti karta tha, isliye 'Data' aur 'data' alag gine jate the. V2 me normalization pehle hoti hai, iske baad hi koi analysis chalti hai — isliye numbers comparable hote hain.

projects.realWorld: RAG pipeline ka ingestion aur retrieval stage isi shape ka hota hai: normalize → keyword/semantic index → similarity search → structured report; aur top-N score ke saath keyword extraction monitoring dashboards me bhi use hota hai.

interview.q: Is system ko 1 lakh documents par kaise scale karoge?
interview.a: SequenceMatcher O(n·m) hai isliye naive pairwise comparison scale nahi karta. Pehle inverted index se candidates filter karo, aur semantic retrieval ke liye embeddings + ANN (HNSW/FAISS) use karo; similarity sirf shortlisted docs par chalao.

interview.q: Time aur space complexity kya hai?
interview.a: Normalization O(total characters), keywords O(tokens) with O(vocab) memory, similarity har pair par O(len(a)·len(b)) worst case. Corpus-level memory tokens ke sum ke proportional hai.

interview.q: Error handling kaise kiya aur kya miss ho sakta hai?
interview.a: Type aur empty-corpus cases handle hue aur warning log hoti hai. Miss: partial input (truncated UTF-8), aur bahut bada document — uske liye streaming/tokenizer limits chahiye.

interview.q: Is project ko API me kaise convert karoge?
interview.a: report() aur similarity() pure functions hain, isliye FastAPI me POST /analyze (docs list) aur POST /similar (doc + corpus) wrap kar dunga; heavy embedding step alag worker me rakhunga, aur Pydantic se input validation aur response schema dunga.

interviewTasks.q: Whiteboard: 'String ek palindrome hai, sirf alphanumeric characters consider karte hue' — interview me code likho aur edge cases batao.
interviewTasks.a: Normalization (lower + isalnum filter) ke baad two-pointer compare karo — O(n) time, O(1) extra space. Edge cases: empty string (True), single character (True), Unicode digits, aur bahut lambi string.

interviewTasks.q: Interview me diya gaya: 'Ek string me sabse pehla character batao jo sirf ek baar aaya hai.' Live code likho.
interviewTasks.a: Counter se counts lo aur string par dobara chalo; pehla character jiska count 1 ho, wahi answer. Complexity O(n) time, O(k) space. Agar akshar sirf a-z hain to 26-length array use kar sakte hain.

interviewTasks.q: Practical task: do documents ka similarity score nikalo aur threshold ke saath 'duplicate' flag do.
interviewTasks.a: difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio() 0..1 score deta hai; normalize karne ke baad compare karna zaroori hai warna case/formatting se score girta hai. Threshold (jaise 0.85) business decision hai — isliye config me rakho aur logs me score print karo.

interviewTasks.q: Interview me poocha jaye: 'CSV ka ek column galat parse ho raha hai, debugging kaise karoge?' — approach likho.
interviewTasks.a: Pehle problematic row isolate karo (minimal reproduction), us row ke raw bytes/whitespace check karo, split ke separator aur quoting dekho, phir csv module vs manual split ka farq test karo. Fix ke saath ek regression test add karo.

interviewTasks.q: Coding round: prompt template banao jo {context} aur {question} ko fill kare aur missing keys par clear error de.
interviewTasks.a: str.format_map ke saath ek dict pass karo jo missing keys par custom error raise kare, ya string.Template use karo ($context) aur substitute() se KeyError catch karo. Templating se prompt injection ka risk kam hota hai kyunki template code se aata hai, user input se nahi.

revision: String immutable hai — har 'change' nayi string banata hai (isliye loop me += nahi, list + join).
Indexing 0-based hai, negative index peeche se, aur slicing me end index exclude hota hai.
Case methods: lower/casefold (comparison), title/capitalize (display), upper (rarely correct for text).
Search methods: find (return -1), index (raise ValueError), startswith/endswith, count.
Cleaning order: strip → case normalize → punctuation remove → whitespace collapse, aur function idempotent rakho.
Formatting: f-string default, .format() runtime template ke liye, logging me lazy % style.
Parity: bytes/str ka fark, encoding UTF-8, raw string regex aur Windows paths ke liye.
